title: Listen and Say First Sounds
summary: Connect a few first Kreyòl words and short phrases with what you hear, then say the same targets aloud using transcript-based speaking practice.

sketchBlocks.title: Let the full word come before analysis
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
When a new language is unfamiliar, it is tempting to break every word into English-looking pieces. Instead, listen to the **whole Kreyòl word**, then connect it with the spelling you already saw.

Use these anchors:

- **bonjou**
- **mèsi**
- **wi**

Replay whenever you need to. Focus on recognizing the whole word first; speed will come later. Then listen for one more short word and rebuild what you hear.

sketchBlocks.title: Use the written target as your speaking guide
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Read the whole word once, listen to how it sounds, then say it naturally. Keep your attention on the complete word instead of trying to pronounce it one letter at a time.

Keep the word intact. For example, when you see **mèsi**, preserve the word as one unit instead of spelling it aloud letter by letter.

sketchBlocks.title: Hear words together
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Once a single word feels familiar, listen to two words together. A short phrase such as **Wi, mèsi.** lets you hear familiar Kreyòl without adding much new vocabulary.

Listen first, rebuild what you heard, then say the same phrase. This creates a direct path from sound → written Kreyòl → spoken Kreyòl.

quizDraft.prompt: Which spelling matches the Kreyòl greeting you heard in this lesson?
